no_rule_decisions.reason: Walks the z/OS TIOT control block and DISPLAYs each DD name with 'valid UCB' or 'null UCB'; diagnostic output only, no effect on processing.
Technical state machine: WS-FL-DD selects which file to open next via ALTER/GO TO (TRNXFILE, XREFFILE, CUSTFILE, ACCTFILE, then READTRNX loading); OTHER ends the program.
Defensive status check after opening TRNXFILE: return codes '00' or '04' accepted, otherwise abend.
Defensive status check after reading the first TRNXFILE record: '00' or '04' accepted, otherwise abend.
Defensive status check after opening XREFFILE.
Defensive status check after opening CUSTFILE.
Defensive status check after opening ACCTFILE.
Read-loop control for TRNXFILE: '00' loops back to load the next record, '10' ends loading, anything else abends.
Defensive status check after closing TRNXFILE.
Defensive status check after closing XREFFILE.
Defensive status check after closing CUSTFILE.
Defensive status check after closing ACCTFILE.

observations.text: The in-memory transaction table holds at most 51 cards x 10 transactions (WS-CARD-TBL OCCURS 51, WS-TRAN-TBL OCCURS 10), but 8500-READTRNX-READ increments CR-CNT and TR-CNT with no bounds check; larger transaction files overwrite storage beyond the table.

Control flow uses ALTER and GO TO (8100-FILE-OPEN is altered to the next open paragraph) and a hand-built state machine driven by WS-FL-DD; the header states these constructs are deliberately included to exercise modernization tooling.

PSA-BLOCK is addressed through PSAPTR, which is never set (null pointer, i.e. absolute address 0 where the z/OS PSA resides); the program then chains PSA+536 to the TCB and TCB+12 to the TIOT. This is platform-specific control-block access with no portable equivalent.
The HTML statement header hardcodes the bank name and address 'Bank of XYZ', '410 Terry Ave N', 'Seattle WA 99999'.
STMT-FILE and HTML-FILE have no FILE STATUS clause; their OPEN, WRITE and CLOSE results are never checked.
9999-ABEND-PROGRAM calls CEE3ABD with no abend code or timing parameters.

Statements are produced per card cross-reference record, not per account; an account with several cards gets one statement per card, each showing the full account balance but only that card's transactions (Inferred from the XREFFILE-driven main loop and card-number matching).

paragraphs.logic: Addresses the PSA, TCB and TIOT control blocks, displays the job and step name and every DD name from the TIOT with its UCB status, then opens STMT-FILE and HTML-FILE for output and initializes the transaction table and counters. Falls through into 0000-START.
paragraphs.name: (PROCEDURE DIVISION entry)

paragraphs.logic: Dispatches on WS-FL-DD: for TRNXFILE, XREFFILE, CUSTFILE or ACCTFILE it ALTERs 8100-FILE-OPEN to the matching open paragraph and GOes TO it; 'READTRNX' goes to 8500-READTRNX-READ; any other value goes to 9999-GOBACK.
paragraphs.name: 0000-START

paragraphs.logic: Loops until END-OF-FILE = 'Y': reads the next cross-reference record and, if found, reads the customer and account, writes the statement header, resets WS-TOTAL-AMT and writes the card's transactions and totals. Then closes TRNXFILE, XREFFILE, CUSTFILE, ACCTFILE (through CBSTM03B) and STMT-FILE/HTML-FILE.
paragraphs.name: 1000-MAINLINE

paragraphs.logic: GOBACK - ends the program.
paragraphs.name: 9999-GOBACK

paragraphs.logic: Calls CBSTM03B to read the next XREFFILE record. RC '00' continues, '10' sets END-OF-FILE 'Y', any other displays 'ERROR READING XREFFILE' with the return code and abends. Moves the returned data to CARD-XREF-RECORD.
paragraphs.name: 1000-XREFFILE-GET-NEXT

paragraphs.logic: Calls CBSTM03B for a keyed read of CUSTFILE with XREF-CUST-ID (key length = length of XREF-CUST-ID). RC other than '00' displays 'ERROR READING CUSTFILE' and abends; otherwise moves the data to CUSTOMER-RECORD.
paragraphs.name: 2000-CUSTFILE-GET

paragraphs.logic: Calls CBSTM03B for a keyed read of ACCTFILE with XREF-ACCT-ID. RC other than '00' displays 'ERROR READING ACCTFILE' and abends; otherwise moves the data to ACCOUNT-RECORD.
paragraphs.name: 3000-ACCTFILE-GET

paragraphs.logic: Scans the card table until past CR-CNT or a table card number greater than XREF-CARD-NUM; for the matching card, writes every stored transaction via 6000-WRITE-TRANS and adds TRNX-AMT to WS-TOTAL-AMT. Then writes the 'Total EXP:' total line and end-of-statement line to STMT-FILE and the closing HTML rows and tags to HTML-FILE.
paragraphs.name: 4000-TRNXFILE-GET

paragraphs.logic: Initializes STATEMENT-LINES, writes the start banner and HTML header, builds ST-NAME from first, middle and last names and ST-ADD3 from address line 3, state, country and ZIP, moves address lines 1-2, ACCT-ID, ACCT-CURR-BAL and CUST-FICO-CREDIT-SCORE, writes the HTML name/address/basic-details block and then the plain-text header lines 1-13.
paragraphs.name: 5000-CREATE-STATEMENT

paragraphs.logic: Writes the fixed HTML document header (DOCTYPE, head, table), the 'Statement for Account Number:' heading with ACCT-ID, and the bank name/address block.
paragraphs.name: 5100-WRITE-HTML-HEADER

paragraphs.logic: End of the 5100 PERFORM THRU range (EXIT).
paragraphs.name: 5100-EXIT

paragraphs.logic: Writes FD-HTMLFILE-REC lines for the statement header: ST-NAME (via L23-NAME) in a 16px paragraph, then ST-ADD1, ST-ADD2 and ST-ADD3 through HTML-ADDR-LN; the 'Account ID', 'Current Balance' and 'FICO Score' lines built from ST-ACCT-ID, ST-CURR-BAL and ST-FICO-SCORE through HTML-BSIC-LN; and fixed table markup by SETting 88-levels of HTML-FIXED-LN (HTML-LTDE, HTML-LTRE, HTML-LTRS, HTML-L22-35, HTML-L30-42) including HTML-L43 'Transaction Summary' and the column headings HTML-L48 'Tran ID', HTML-L51 'Tran Details' and HTML-L54 'Amount'.
paragraphs.name: 5200-WRITE-HTML-NMADBS

paragraphs.logic: End of the 5200 PERFORM THRU range (EXIT).
paragraphs.name: 5200-EXIT

paragraphs.logic: Moves TRNX-ID, TRNX-DESC and TRNX-AMT to statement line 14 and writes it to STMT-FILE, then writes an HTML table row with the same three values.
paragraphs.name: 6000-WRITE-TRANS

paragraphs.logic: ALTERable GO TO target; initially GO TO 8100-TRNXFILE-OPEN, redirected by 0000-START to the next file-open paragraph.
paragraphs.name: 8100-FILE-OPEN

paragraphs.logic: Opens TRNXFILE and reads its first record through CBSTM03B (abend unless RC '00' or '04'), saves the card number in WS-SAVE-CARD, sets CR-CNT 1 and TR-CNT 0, sets WS-FL-DD to 'READTRNX' and returns to 0000-START.
paragraphs.name: 8100-TRNXFILE-OPEN

paragraphs.logic: Opens XREFFILE through CBSTM03B (abend unless RC '00' or '04'), sets WS-FL-DD to 'CUSTFILE' and returns to 0000-START.
paragraphs.name: 8200-XREFFILE-OPEN

paragraphs.logic: Opens CUSTFILE through CBSTM03B (abend unless RC '00' or '04'), sets WS-FL-DD to 'ACCTFILE' and returns to 0000-START.
paragraphs.name: 8300-CUSTFILE-OPEN

paragraphs.logic: Opens ACCTFILE through CBSTM03B (abend unless RC '00' or '04') and GOes TO 1000-MAINLINE.
paragraphs.name: 8400-ACCTFILE-OPEN

paragraphs.logic: Stores the current transaction in WS-TRNX-TABLE: same card as WS-SAVE-CARD increments TR-CNT, a new card saves the previous count in WS-TRCT, increments CR-CNT and restarts TR-CNT at 1. Reads the next TRNXFILE record through CBSTM03B and loops on RC '00', goes to 8599-EXIT on '10', abends otherwise.
paragraphs.name: 8500-READTRNX-READ

paragraphs.logic: Saves the last card's transaction count in WS-TRCT(CR-CNT), sets WS-FL-DD to 'XREFFILE' and returns to 0000-START.
paragraphs.name: 8599-EXIT

paragraphs.logic: Closes TRNXFILE through CBSTM03B; abends with 'ERROR CLOSING TRNXFILE' unless RC '00' or '04'.
paragraphs.name: 9100-TRNXFILE-CLOSE

paragraphs.logic: Closes XREFFILE through CBSTM03B; abends with 'ERROR CLOSING XREFFILE' unless RC '00' or '04'.
paragraphs.name: 9200-XREFFILE-CLOSE

paragraphs.logic: Closes CUSTFILE through CBSTM03B; abends with 'ERROR CLOSING CUSTFILE' unless RC '00' or '04'.
paragraphs.name: 9300-CUSTFILE-CLOSE

paragraphs.logic: Closes ACCTFILE through CBSTM03B; abends with 'ERROR CLOSING ACCTFILE' unless RC '00' or '04'.
paragraphs.name: 9400-ACCTFILE-CLOSE

paragraphs.logic: Displays 'ABENDING PROGRAM' and calls CEE3ABD without parameters.
paragraphs.name: 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM

rules.conditions: TRNX-CARD-NUM equal to / different from WS-SAVE-CARD.
rules.outcome: WS-CARD-NUM, WS-TRAN-NUM, WS-TRAN-REST and WS-TRCT populated; CR-CNT = number of cards.
rules.statement: Before any statement is produced, all transactions are loaded into a two-dimensional in-memory table grouped by card number: consecutive transactions with the same TRNX-CARD-NUM are stored under one card entry, and a change of card number starts a new card entry. The table holds up to 51 cards with up to 10 transactions each.

rules.conditions: WS-CARD-NUM(CR-JMP) = XREF-CARD-NUM; search ends when CR-JMP > CR-CNT or WS-CARD-NUM(CR-JMP) > XREF-CARD-NUM.
rules.outcome: Each matching transaction written as a detail line (text and HTML).
rules.statement: A statement lists only the transactions whose card number equals the cross-reference card number being processed. The table search stops at the first table card number greater than the cross-reference card, which assumes both files are in ascending card-number order (TRNXFILE is keyed by card number + transaction id in CBSTM03B).
The statement total ('Total EXP:') is the sum of TRNX-AMT of all transactions listed for the card; it is reset to zero for each cross-reference record.

rules.conditions: WS-M03B-RC not '00' after customer or account keyed read; not '00'/'10' after cross-reference read.
rules.outcome: 'ERROR READING CUSTFILE' / 'ERROR READING ACCTFILE' / 'ERROR READING XREFFILE', return code display, abend via CEE3ABD.
rules.statement: Every card cross-reference must resolve to an existing customer (XREF-CUST-ID) and account (XREF-ACCT-ID); if either keyed read fails, or the cross-reference read fails other than end of file, the statement run abends instead of skipping the card.

rules.outcome: ST-NAME, ST-ADD1..3, ST-ACCT-ID, ST-CURR-BAL, ST-FICO-SCORE in text and HTML output.
rules.statement: The statement header shows the customer name as first, middle and last name each truncated at the first space and separated by single spaces, address lines 1 and 2, a third address line combining address line 3, state, country and ZIP, plus account id, current balance and FICO score.

rules.conditions: Each XREFFILE record read with RC '00'.
rules.outcome: Statement header, transaction lines and total written to STMTFILE and HTMLFILE.
rules.statement: One statement (text and HTML) is produced for every record in the card cross-reference file, in cross-reference order, until end of file.

sme_questions.question: Should statements be produced per account (aggregating all cards) instead of per card cross-reference record?
What are the real volume limits for the statement run? The table allows only 51 cards and 10 transactions per card with no overflow check.
Why is CBSTM03B return code '04' accepted as success on open, first read and close? Which condition is expected to produce it?

summary.text: CBSTM03A is the batch account-statement program; it writes each statement in two formats, an 80-byte plain-text file (STMTFILE) and a 100-byte HTML file (HTMLFILE). All file access goes through subroutine CBSTM03B. It first displays the job's DD names from the z/OS TIOT, then uses an ALTER/GO TO state machine to open the transaction file, load every transaction into an in-memory table grouped by card number (max 51 cards x 10 transactions), and open the cross-reference, customer and account files. For each card cross-reference record it reads the customer and account by key, writes a statement header (name, address, account id, balance, FICO score), lists that card's transactions and prints their total. Read failures for cross-reference, customer or account abend the run. The header says the program deliberately uses control-block addressing, ALTER/GO TO, COMP/COMP-3, a 2-D array and a subroutine call to exercise modernization tooling.
